artworks.title: "Do Not Sit on the Grain Measure" [fol. 12 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing depicting a medieval scene with allegorical elements. The drawing features a house labeled "Vita domus humanae" with figures interacting. One figure labeled "Hodie" is serving a drink to another person, while outside, a figure labeled "Cras" is entering as a figure labeled "Tempus" gestures. The house has a tiled roof and the label "Indulencia" is present. The figures wear medieval European clothing and the artwork utilizes strong line work and shading to convey depth and texture.

artworks.title: Credulity Preparing to Nurse the Mother of Hope [fol. 18 verso]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure on a horse followed by a person in a blindfolded state. The drawing shows a person atop a horse with flowing hair and an unclothed torso. The horse is decorated and stands on a slope. Below and slightly to the right of the horse, a blindfolded person in robes holds their hands in front of them. Above the mounted figure, there is an unfurling scroll with text, and another scroll near the standing person's feet with additional text. The lines and shading indicate a detailed image.

artworks.title: Hope, Reaching for Heaven, Stands among Sad and Happy Men, Joys, and Fear [fol. 19 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of allegorical figures representing various states of mind or virtues. The image depicts a central figure pointing upwards to a banner that reads "Meta Summi Boni." On either side are groups of figures labeled with different emotions or states like ‘Tristes’ to the left and ‘Gaudia’ to the right. Below are other figures with banners like ‘Timor’ and ‘Lest’. The intricate linework emphasizes detailed expressions and clothing styles, suggesting a historical or allegorical scene. The drawing uses fine detailing and shading to emphasize the figures' emotions and interactions.

artworks.title: An Ape in Purple with a Sick Man, a Good Man, and a Miser [fol. 36 verso]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This painting depicts an allegorical scene with a reclining figure on a bed, a tree bearing fruit, and three clothed figures. The scene includes a nude figure on a bed draped with flowing fabric labeled "Eger", a tree with fruit, a figure in red holding a basket, and two figures in robes with labels "Avarus" and "In Virtute Fortis." At the bottom, there is a Latin inscription. The illustration combines figurative elements with a possible satirical or allegorical theme. This artwork is reminiscent of the Renaissance period like Albrecht Dürer's style.

artworks.title: "Do Not Have Swallows under the Same Roof" [fol. 40 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a painting of birds and insects near a building. The scene depicts swallows flying around an architectural frame decorated with vines, surrounded by large flies. At the bottom of the structure, there are storks interacting with a figure holding a tray of fish. The birds and insects are dynamic in their movement, contrasting with the geometric stability of the architecture. The use of muted earth tones and precise lines suggests this is a manuscript illustration from an earlier period.

artworks.title: "Do Not Eat Beans" [fol. 25 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: Drawn using pen and brown ink on cream-colored paper, a robed man to our right holds up both hands and looks away from a plant in this vertical composition. A hood covers the man’s head, and he has a long beard. His hands shield his face from the plant to our left, which is painted with watercolor to give it green leaves and stems and dark pink flowers. A handwritten name above the man reads, "Pythagoras." The plant is labeled “Fabe.” A crack splits the ground from the bottom right corner of the paper across the page.

artworks.title: "Do Not Wear a Tight-Fitting Ring" [fol. 23 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a group of figures interacting around a central figure wearing a costume with ears on the headpiece. The central figure stands with a rigid pose, wearing a detailed costume, while other figures surround it. The figures are engaged in altering or repairing the central character's attire, each with a focused demeanor. The style of the drawing reflects an intricate attention to the form and detail of the figures' clothing and poses, displaying techniques reminiscent of medieval European art.

artworks.title: "Turn aside the Sharp Sword" [fol. 44 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image shows two figures: a small child holding a sword and an adult dressed in medieval-style clothing. The child has round facial features and tight curls, while the adult wears a pointed hat with a long feather. The adult is slightly bent forward toward the child, who is looking up at them. The adult's attire includes textured fabric and what appears to be tassels. The background is plain with minimal details, suggesting a rocky ground.

artworks.title: "Do Not Break the Crown" [fol. 43 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and black ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a armored figure holding a sword in a striking stance. The figure is barefoot and dressed in a tunic-like attire with intricate details. On the ground, there is a sword scabbard. In the background, there are two crowns on a hill. The ground has wavy lines, and the image is rendered with fine lines to create depth and shadows.

artworks.title: "Do Not Poke the Fire with a Sword" [fol. 20 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and gray ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a knight standing next to a fire. The knight is depicted in medieval armor, holding a sword in one hand and extending the other hand with a stick towards the fire. The fire consists of large logs and swirling flames. The knight's pose is dynamic, suggesting action or readiness. The ground appears rocky or uneven. The drawing is composed of fine lines and shading, displaying intricate details of the knight's attire and the fire. The style is illustrative and detailed, characteristic of Renaissance sketches.

artworks.title: "You Are Tying a Dolphin by the Tail" [fol. 17 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and black ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a kneeling figure with a fantastical creature emerging from water. The figure is dressed in a long, flowing garment with distinct, pointed headwear characteristic of a jester's cap. They are kneeling on a sloped ground, interacting with the creature. The creature resembles a mythical sea dragon with a sinuous body and ornate scales, emerging from a body of water that is subtly hinted at with a few undulating lines. The lines are delicate and the shading soft. The background is largely unadorned.

artworks.title: A Fool Feeding Flowers to Swine [fol. 42 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image shows a figure feeding pigs. The individual has animal ears and is pouring apples into a trough, while three pigs are eating. The figure is dressed in period-style clothing with a hood, and the pigs are of varying sizes. The pigs are engaged with the food, and the scene is drawn with detailed and delicate style, highlighting the features of both the figure and the pigs. The artwork portrays a pastoral moment, depicting agrarian life and the interaction between humans and animals.

artworks.title: "Do Not Put Food in a Chamber Pot" [fol. 24 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image depicts a person in a jester's outfit standing on a raised platform. The individual is pouring liquid from a pitcher into a container. The jester has medium-toned skin and wears a jester's hat with three pointed ends and bells. The attire is decorated with additional bells. The background is a plain, textured surface.

artworks.title: "Feed Not Things That Have Sharp Claws" [fol. 38 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image shows a figure in a lion's den feeding or battling the lions. The setting is a hexagonal arena with the central figure, covered with a red hood and a sleeveless garment, holding a piece of meat towards a pack of lions. One lion reaches towards the figure with an open mouth, while others surround the figure in a dynamic stance. The walls of the enclosure have architectural designs, with a barred door or window at the lower section, and trees with green foliage outside. The artwork features detailed lines and muted earth tones, resembling medieval manuscript illuminations.

artworks.title: "Speak Not Against the Sun" and "Do Not Make Water Facing the Sun" [fol. 39 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor and stylus on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner

artworks.title: The Calumny of Apelles [fol. 6 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor and stylus on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image depicts several figures within a structured setting. The focus is on a seated individual on a throne-like chair, exhibiting full body length in a seated position. There are multiple figures surrounding this central person, with varied body parts shown, several on bent knees or standing, directed towards the seated figure. The seated person has long hair, possibly depicted with a crown or headdress, and is wearing a blue robe with red footwear, holding an orb. Around them are figures with different facial features and hair color; some of them exhibit head coverings or hairstyles that suggest medieval or religious attire. These individuals wear robes in a variety of colors, including red, blue, orange, and green, many of which are intricately patterned or textured. One of the figures holds a long staff. The setting appears indoors, with an arched alcove resembling a decorative niche in the background, flanked by columns, and a mosaic pattern. Behind, a fruit-bearing tree emerges, adding verdant contrast to the scene. The flooring consists of a blue tiled pattern defining the area of the scene.

artworks.title: "You Are Shooting at Heaven" [fol. 9 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image shows a landscape with a low horizon line, featuring a church, lush foliage, rolling hills, and a central figure of an archer with scattered arrows. The artwork has detailed linework in a monochromatic color palette of brown tones, resembling an ink or pen-and-ink drawing. The sky above the landscape includes stylized clouds, stars, a sun with rays, and a half-moon with a face.

artworks.title: The Statue of Opportunity, a Passer-by, and Remorse [fol. 8r]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a mythical scene featuring figures and structures. The image shows a figure standing on a winged platform on top of a mechanical wheel, holding symbolic items like a crescent moon and an armillary sphere. The wheel is mounted on a spire-like column, and below, another figure in traditional attire gestures upwards. To the right, a tower with a person peeking through an arched window is depicted. Latin text encircles the scene. The drawing style is similar to early manuscript illustrations with detailed line work.

artworks.title: The Statue of Opportunity and the Passer-by [fol. 8 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a figure standing in front of a castle-like structure with a winged figure on top. The image shows a building resembling a castle with two cylindrical towers topped with flags and a pointed roof in the center. The entrance is an arched doorway, and the front facade features decorative architectural elements. In the foreground, a smaller figure appears to be looking up at the structure, holding a staff or a long object. Above the building, a winged person stands on a platform, holding a globe and another spherical object. The drawing includes text around the central image, which seems to be written in a stylized medieval script. The background is plain, with no additional elements, emphasizing the figures and the structure.

artworks.title: Allegory of the Life of a Scholar in a Rich Household [fol. 3 verso / 4 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of a medieval allegorical scene. The image shows a group of figures within a walled enclosure, looking upwards toward an emblem with a seated figure holding symbols of authority. Below the platform, there are skeletal figures and others with disturbing features. The composition includes detailed architecture and flowing garments, with expressive postures and gestures. The entire scene is etched with fine lines, creating an intricate visual narrative.

artworks.title: "Obliterate the Trace of the Pot in the Ashes" [fol. 32 verso / 33 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor, heightened with gold on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a painting of an allegorical scene in the style of a Renaissance artist. It is rich in detail, with figures representing various virtues and vices. The scene is divided into sections, with each figure holding a banner inscribed with Latin text. On the left side is a crucifixion scene with figures labeled as virtues such as "Oblivio," "Charitas," and "Vindicta." The right side features figures symbolizing vices or traits like “Crudelitas,” “Voluptas,” and “Cupiditas.” In the center, there is an enthroned figure with a banner reading "Principis Clementis," possibly symbolizing clemency or justice. A flaming central figure holds a shield-like item. The overall composition is reminiscent of manuscript illustrations portraying moral lessons or religious stories through allegorical figures.

artworks.title: "Do Not Turn Back When You Arrive at the End" [fol. 26 verso / 27 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on two joined sheets of  laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: This is a drawing of an allegorical medieval theme. The artwork depicts a scene filled with symbolism. On the left side, a house labeled "Domus Hominis Prudentis" (House of the Wise Man) is shown, with figures labeled as "Cupiditas Vitæ," "Medicus," "Pharmacopoia," and "Ratio." The right side features mythical figures such as "Vir," "Prudes," and "Finis Vitæ." This side includes a mythical creature, a somber figure in a chariot, a figure labeled "Saturnus," and an armored knight labeled "Mars."

artworks.title: Personification of Friendship (Amicitia) [fol. 2 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image shows a young woman standing with a slight lean to her right. She has long, flowing light-colored hair, wearing red and beige robes with her chest partially exposed, touching an injury on her chest. She wears a headband with a central element across her forehead, and is barefoot on a plain, off-white parchment background with faint handwritten text.

artworks.title: "Do Not Make Water on Clippings from Nails or Hair" [fol. 30 recto]
artworks.medium: pen and brown ink with watercolor on laid paper
artworks.creditLine: Woodner Collection, Gift of Andrea Woodner
artworks.description: The image shows two figures against a plain background. On the left, a person is kneeling and presenting a large chalice. This person has a youthful face, curly hair, and wears a robe. On the right, another person is leaning forward toward the chalice. This person has a bearded face, long hair, and wears an elaborate robe. A stream of red flows from the chalice towards their mouth.
